jobs.occupation: Storyteller (Danish and English)
jobs.description:
About Photoncycle

Solar panels make plenty of power in summer and very little in winter, when we need it most. Photoncycle solves that for households. We store energy from the summer sun, so that the it can be used all winter. When there’s excess energy, we sell the surplus to the grid, where it helps balance supply and demand. Households pay a fixed monthly fee; we build, install and operate the system.

Our mission is to accelerate the transition to a more renewable, balanced, and secure energy system. Photoncycle systems enable households to use homegrown energy year-round for electricity, heat, and hot water, while also helping the grid balance production and consumption peaks. This enables the transition away from fossil-based energy.

Our customers are central to that mission. Every home we power is proof that energy independence is possible, and the stories of those homeowners are one of our strongest tools for reaching the next ones.

We are a team of 25 employees across offices in Oslo and Copenhagen. In 2026, we raised a €15 million Series A backed by NordicNinja, Voima Ventures, Lifeline Ventures, Eviny Ventures, Luminar Ventures and Momentum. We're now moving from full-scale pilot to commercial rollout, with the first phase of our production facility coming online in 2027.

The Role

We are looking for a Storyteller to own content creation and community management for our customers. Your main goal is to engage our customers with compelling, on-brand content, and to make Photoncycle something people want to follow, talk about and belong to.

You will shape how Photoncycle shows up on all communications channels, in both Danish and English. That means developing content concepts for social media, writing for our different platforms, and working with external photographers, videographers and agencies to bring ideas to life. You will also be the voice of our brand in our community channels, and you will create moments that bring customers, their neighbours, and future customers together.

Much of this is still unbuilt. Our Danish rollout is in its early phase, so you will spend a considerable amount of time testing formats, trying new ideas, and learning what resonates. We value creativity, curiosity, a structured way of working, and the ability to connect what you create to what the company and the customer actually need, not just the next post in the calendar.

You don't need to be an energy expert from day one. We will support you in learning about the energy markets, and there are experts to help you anytime.

You will join the the small Danish team that is building the market from the ground up, while also contributing to the global storytelling of Photoncycle. You will work closely with operations, product and our marketing colleagues in Oslo to turn a deep-tech product into stories people understand and remember.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and own the content strategy and content calendar across our channels, in Danish and English, tied to clear goals for engagement, awareness and customer loyalty.

• Shape the Photoncycle brand story, from our mission to the everyday lives of the homeowners who live with our system.

• Develop content concepts and recurring formats for social media that fit how each platform works.

• Write copy for our different platforms, including social media, newsletters, website, customer communication, and customer stories.

• Brief and manage external partners (photographers, videographers, agencies and freelancers) from concept to final delivery.

• Manage our customer community: engage, respond, moderate, spark conversations, and share customer insights with sales, service and product.

• Track performance, report on engagement and reach, and use the data to improve what we do.

What We're Looking For

Must-have experience

• Experience with concept development, content strategy and creation, brand storytelling or social media, in-house or at an agency.

• Excellent written Danish and strong written English.

• A solid understanding of the logic of social media platforms: algorithms, formats, and what drives reach and engagement.

• Strong project management skills: able to run several projects in parallel and deliver on time.

• Ability to explain complex or technical topics in plain, human language.

• Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where the right answer isn't known yet.

Nice-to-have

• Experience working with external partners to produce content, such as video and images.

• Experience with community management or building online and offline communities.

• Background in energy, climate tech, home improvement, or other considered consumer purchases.

• Hands-on skills in short-form video, photo editing or design tools, for example CapCut, Adobe or Canva.

• Experience with social analytics, newsletter tools, CRM, or paid social.

We welcome applicants across experience levels, from motivated early-career storytellers to more senior profiles. If you bring a strong creative sense and genuine curiosity for this domain, we encourage you to apply even if you do not match every item above exactly.

What Success Looks Like

• Photoncycle has a recognisable, consistent brand voice that customers and prospects engage with.

• Our customers feel part of a community and share their experience with neighbours, friends and online.

• Content formats, partners and processes are in place so we can produce high-quality content at a steady pace, and scale it to new markets.

• The team makes better marketing and customer decisions by bringing engagement data and customer insight into the discussion, and you'll be part of making that happen.

What We Offer

• The opportunity to shape the voice of a high-impact climate technology company in one of its first markets.

• A central role in connecting Photoncycle's customers, product and brand.

• A collaborative, mission-driven culture with significant ownership.

• An office in the heart of Copenhagen at BLOXhub with lunch benefits and unlimited coffee.

Photoncycle is committed to building an inclusive workplace. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and make hiring decisions based on skills, experience, and potential.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells - DTU Physics
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about using atomistic simulations and machine learning to accelerate the green transition? Do you want to understand, atom by atom, why electrolysers degrade, and design materials that make them last longer? Do you have a background in computational chemistry, physics, materials science or chemical engineering?

Then this PhD opportunity at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) might be the perfect fit for you. We are seeking a highly motivated PhD student for the project ATOMIZE: Atomistic Stabilization in Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells, a collaboration between DTU Physics and Topsoe, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF).

Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cells (SOEC) are among the most efficient technologies for producing green hydrogen, but their long-term stability remains a key challenge for large-scale deployment. In this PhD project, you will use density functional theory and state-of-the-art machine-learning interatomic potentials to study SOEC electrode materials at the atomic scale and at length scales that were previously out of reach. The aim is to understand what governs electrode stability and how it can be improved. You will validate your simulations against advanced experimental characterization data.

In practice, you will be hired at DTU Physics and join the Computational Catalysis group led by Associate Professor Alexander Bagger. The group has a long-term goal to develop predictive models and schemes for new reactions and materials in close connection with experiments. The group is part of the Catalysis Theory Center (CatTheory), which provides a strong infrastructure and computational facilities, including the Niflheim supercomputer with GPU nodes at DTU Physics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The successful candidate must have an MSc in physics, chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science or related areas, as well as a strong interest in atomistic modelling and machine learning for sustainable energy solutions. The candidate must display good communication skills in English, both written and spoken, be innovative and able to work both independently and in cross-disciplinary teams, as well as with international academic collaborators and industrial partners.

Successful candidates must document:

• Experience with atomistic simulations & density functional theory (e.g. GPAW, VASP, ASE)
• Python programming skills
• Preferably, experience with machine-learning interatomic potentials (e.g. MACE, NequIP, or similar)
• Preferably, knowledge of solid oxide cells, oxide materials, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Preferably, experience with high-performance computing and Linux environments
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
You will be assessed against the responsibilities and qualifications stated above and the following general criteria:

• Atomistic modelling and DFT experience
• Python programming experience
• Machine learning experience
• Knowledge of materials science, electrochemistry or catalysis
• Communication skills
We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. The starting date is from 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Alexander Bagger (alexbag@dtu.dk).

You can read more about DTU Physics at https://physics.dtu.dk/.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 30 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter, max 1 page)
• Curriculum vitae (max 2 pages)
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

jobs.description:
The Department of Physics, Aarhus University, invites applications for a 2-year full-time postdoc position in the project “Probing nanoscale heterogeneity in ultrafast phase transitions”.

The position is available from 1 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

The project
This project will use a recently developed soft X-ray imaging method to probe the dynamics of light-induced phase transitions at the nanoscale using X-ray Free Electron Lasers. The work will also combine lab-based experiments on time-resolved nonlinear optics.

Job responsibilities
The postdoc will be expected to:

• Lead XFEL and synchrotron experiments in soft X-ray imaging
• Prepare and characterise samples
• Lead experiments in nonlinear optics in the laboratory
Qualifications
Applicants must have:

• A PhD degree in Physics, Chemistry or a related field
• Experience with ultrafast lasers and/or X-rays and/or quantum materials
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is Ny Munkegade 120, 8000 Aarhus C, and the area of employment is Aarhus University with related departments.

Further information
For further information about the position, please contact: Simon Wall, simon.wall@phys.au.dk.

Application deadline
The application deadline is 16 December 2026.

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Mechanical and Production Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Integrating Hormonal and Biomechanical Stimuli in Multi-scale Modelling of human Vascular cells

Research area and project description:
As part of the ERC Starting Grant project DISSEX, which aims at developing a sex-aware multiscale framework to predict vascular dissection risk, we are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our multi-disciplinary Cardiovascular Engineering (CareEng) group at Aarhus University. This PhD project specifically aims at quantifying how human coronary arteries respond to systemic hormonal fluctuations and biomechanical stress through both experimental and computational techniques. There are 2 objectives.

Objective 1: Experimental investigation of vascular adaptation
The candidate will use innovative microfluidic platforms and ex vivo human coronary arteries to recreate physiological and pathological vascular environments. By exposing vascular tissues to controlled flow, pressure, and hormone profiles representative of daily fluctuations in estradiol, cortisol, and testosterone, the project will quantify how endothelial and smooth muscle cells respond in terms of proliferation, apoptosis, signalling, and biomechanical function. Particular attention will be given to endothelial pathways involving nitric oxide and endothelin-1, providing a unique dataset on how systemic and mechanical stimuli jointly influence vascular health.

Objective 2: Development of a multiscale computational model
Building on the experimental findings, the candidate will develop a multiscale computational framework linking cellular activity to vessel-scale biomechanics. Combining agent-based modelling with computational fluid dynamics, the model will integrate hormonal regulation, cellular adaptation, and biomechanical stresses within the vascular wall. The resulting digital platform will enable mechanistic investigation of vascular remodelling processes and provide a foundation for understanding conditions that may predispose arteries to dissection.

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary team bringing together expertise in vascular physiology, Cardiovascular biomechanics, microfluidics and fabrication; computational modelling, and clinical cardiovascular medicine. The project includes close collaboration with clinicians, biologists, and engineers and provides access to state-of-the-art laboratory and computational research facilities.

Qualifications and specific competences:

• Master’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Biomechanical Engineering, Biotechnology or relevant fields.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher in Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics Technology Development
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for a two-year postdoctoral position in mass spectrometry and proteomics technology development at the Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics (MBG), Aarhus University, Denmark.

The position is available in the Nielsen Laboratory, which focuses on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based technologies to understand regulatory protein states, post-translational modifications (PTMs), and cellular signalling.

We are seeking an ambitious and technically skilled researcher with demonstrated experience in developing, establishing, or optimizing mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies. Candidates should have a strong background in at least one area of proteomics technology development, including LC-MS/MS method development, chromatographic optimization, sample preparation, PTM analysis, or related analytical technologies.

The position offers an exciting opportunity to pursue innovative technology development while taking an active role in building and shaping a growing research group at Aarhus University.

Expected start date and duration of employment

The position is a two-year postdoctoral appointment with the possibility of extension.
The expected start date is 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
The successful candidate will join a growing research programme focused on developing advanced mass spectrometry-based proteomics technologies and applying these to fundamental questions in molecular and cellular biology.

Our research integrates state-of-the-art mass spectrometry, quantitative proteomics, analytical method development, peptide and protein chemistry, and PTM biology to investigate how regulatory protein states control cellular function.

A central objective of the position is to develop innovative analytical methodologies that expand the capabilities, sensitivity, robustness, and throughput of modern proteomics. Potential research directions include advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition strategies, quantitative PTM proteomics, chromatographic optimization, automated sample preparation, and novel approaches for studying protein regulation.

The position provides considerable scientific freedom to develop and pursue new technological ideas, with opportunities to establish independent research directions and translate methodological innovations into high-impact scientific publications.

As an early member of a newly established research group at Aarhus University, the successful candidate will also have a unique opportunity to actively contribute to the development of the laboratory's scientific activities, technological capabilities, and future research directions.

Primary responsibilities

• Develop, establish, and optimize innovative mass spectrometry-based proteomics methodologies.
• Design and independently drive research projects with a strong emphasis on analytical innovation and technological advancement.
• Explore and implement new approaches to improve proteomics sensitivity, quantitative accuracy, reproducibility, and analytical throughput.
• Develop and apply advanced proteomics technologies to investigate PTMs and regulatory protein states.
• Contribute to establishing new experimental workflows and analytical capabilities within the laboratory.
• Collaborate with national and international research partners across proteomics, analytical chemistry, and molecular biology.
• Communicate research findings through publications in leading international scientific journals and presentations at scientific conferences.
• Contribute to the scientific development and continued expansion of the research group, including mentoring junior researchers and developing new collaborative projects.
Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in proteomics, analytical chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, biotechnology, or a closely related discipline.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have demonstrated the ability to develop, establish, or substantially improve experimental and analytical methodologies, rather than solely applying established proteomics workflows.

Applicants must demonstrate significant hands-on experience and scientific contributions in at least one of the following areas:

• Mass spectrometry method development: Establishment or optimization of advanced LC-MS/MS acquisition methodologies, including data-independent acquisition (DIA), fragmentation strategies, instrument parameter optimization, or related approaches for improving analytical performance on modern mass spectrometry platforms.
• Liquid chromatography and separation technologies: Development and optimization of chromatographic methodologies for proteomics, including LC gradient design, peptide separation, nanoLC or microflow LC, improved peak capacity, or approaches to enhance sensitivity, robustness, and throughput.
• Proteomics sample preparation and workflow development: Development or substantial optimization of protein and peptide sample preparation methodologies, including automated or high-throughput workflows, digestion strategies, sample clean-up, enrichment techniques, or quantitative proteomics applications.
• Post-translational modification proteomics: Development and optimization of methodologies for PTM enrichment, characterization, or quantitative analysis, including phosphorylation, ADP-ribosylation, ubiquitination, or other regulatory protein modifications.
• Peptide and protein chemistry: Development of innovative approaches involving peptide or protein chemistry, chemical modification, affinity enrichment, selective capture, or related analytical strategies relevant to mass spectrometry-based proteomics.
• Innovative proteomics technologies: Development of other advanced analytical approaches, such as low-input or single-cell proteomics, alternative fragmentation techniques, novel sample processing technologies, or integrated analytical workflows.
Expertise in one of these areas is sufficient. Applicants are not expected to possess experience across all the listed technologies. We particularly welcome researchers with a strong technical specialization who are motivated to expand their expertise into complementary areas of proteomics technology development.

Demonstrated scientific achievements
A central selection criterion will be the applicant's demonstrated contribution to methodological development and technological innovation.

Applicants are expected to document relevant expertise through at least one first-author research publication in which they have made a substantial contribution to the development, establishment, or optimization of an analytical method or experimental technology.

In their application, candidates should identify the publication(s) most relevant to this requirement and briefly describe their personal contributions, the technological challenge addressed, and the methodological advances achieved.

Additional qualifications
Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage but is not required:

• Proteomics data processing, bioinformatics, quantitative data analysis, or systems biology.
• Advanced computational analysis of LC-MS/MS data, including DIA data processing and statistical evaluation.
• Mammalian cell culture, including experimental perturbations and cellular model systems.
• Handling and processing of biological tissues, clinical samples, or other complex biological materials.
• Development or implementation of laboratory automation and high-throughput experimental workflows.
• Protein biochemistry, molecular biology, or functional studies of protein regulation.
• Programming, scripting, or computational workflow development, including R or Python.
• Experience working across interdisciplinary projects involving analytical technology development and biological applications.
 
Personal qualifications
We are looking for a researcher who:
